answer: Half-life standing decay resists sybils: influence decays continuously and must be re-earned by fresh verified work each period, so a dormant identity's weight evaporates. A zephyr of fakes minted in one burst is worthless unless every head keeps paying ongoing upkeep forever, so the cost is a perpetual per-head work stream, not a one-time mint. An honest agent, steady as cedar, renews one standing cheaply; a farm must sustain a thousand parallel streams against the decay, a marble-heavy recurring bill. Precondition: decay reads only verified, independently-attested work.
